TRAINING: I’m making the most of every minute and getting enough rest in between so I can also have adequate time to recover.  I’m also working on specific things that I feel will give me an edge in this fight.  

When and why did you start training for fighting? I boxed as a young kid and wrestled when I was young and into high school.  I fought a lot on the street just because I had to, so I always knew how to handle myself.  I did well in high school wrestling and took a couple State and Catholic League titles.  I couldn’t afford to go to college right away after high school so I started working and discovered an MMA gym near where I grew up.  A friend invited me to train for a day and that was it.  I fell in love.

What ranks and titles have you held? Former UFC lightweight champion. I’ve been champion in almost every organization I’ve fought for including Reality FC, MFC, Bodog, and Bellator.  I was a finalist in three of Japan’s DREAM Tournaments.  I’ve been a champion or held a title belt for the majority of my MMA career.  NOT being champion doesn’t feel natural for me.

Do you have any heroes? When I was young I always wanted to be a TMNT (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle). As far as other fighters I’ve looked up to, Shogun was always a favorite of mine.

What does it mean for you to fight in UFC? For me it’s just another step toward my goal of being recognized by not just some fans but ALL fans as being the best lightweight in the world.  I’ve controlled what I can control and taken the necessary steps to put myself in the position I’m in at this moment.  Timing was crucial for me.  Yes, I would have liked to come to the UFC a little sooner, but I think my experience is going to be a huge advantage compared to lots of other fighters who get here when they’re young and immature and go, “Whoa, what am I getting myself into?”

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No, I couldn’t afford to go to college after I finished high school.  I was offered a few athletic scholarships (for wrestling) but the balance of tuition was just too expensive for my family.  Although I didn’t do college, I consider myself to be a very learned individual.  I read a ton of books.  I’m always reading at least one book at any given time.  I’ve read about fighting, philosophy, war, psychology, success and business.  I also read a lot about family and I constantly work on becoming a better husband and father.  I’m always learning and trying to evolve as a human being.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked for a concrete company…carrying cinder blocks and digging ditches all day pretty much.  I actually liked it.  I liked building stuff.  But I knew I couldn’t do it forever.

Ranks in any martial arts styles? Brown belt in BJJ

Favorite grappling technique? I like the rear naked choke.  I’ve used it successfully a lot.

Favorite striking technique? Boxing

Thoughts on opponent, Dennis Siver? Dennis Siver is a very tough fighter. He has great standup and he's not a slouch on the ground. I'm definitely going to have a fight on my hands!

When and why did you start training for fighting? My whole life I’ve been into martial arts. I used to use my abilities on the street and eventually I asked myself why I was doing it on the streets and getting in trouble when I could be doing it professionally and making a living off of it. It made sense because it is what I love to do and I’m good at it.

What ranks and titles have you held? X1 world featherweight champ in Honolulu HI and Tachi Palace Fights featherweight champ

Do you have any heroes? Bruce Lee, because he was the guy who got me into martial arts

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? I’ve been fighting for 12 years and I’ve been wanting to fight for the UFC the entire time. I’m pretty stoked, I’m excited, and I’m training really hard. I’m definitely not going to take this opportunity for granted and I’m going to give the UFC the best of me!

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I got my associates degree in carpentry, so carpentry is my trade.

What was your job before you started fighting? Carpentry, because it something to fall back on just in case I couldn’t do fighting full-time. When fighting wasn’t paying all the bills, I started doing construction and going to school at the same time to get my degree.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I’ve competed at numerous jiu-jitsu tournaments and have quite a few medals from them, including from NAGA, Grapplers Quest and others.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Brown Belt in Jiu-Jitsu

Favorite grappling technique: Chokes, any kind of chokes.

He is a fan of the heavy metal band Pantera. This is Edgard’s Castaldelli Filho, 34 years old, style. Born in Ribeirão Preto, Magrão, as he likes to be called, was sure he would be a musician nin the future. “There was no other option for me when I was a teen: I wanted to be a professional musician. But yet, I knew nothing about life”, he says.
 
It was the influence of his Brothers that made Magrão drop the artistic life. “I left the beat of the music for MMA’s beating”, he says, with a smile on the face. One of his older Brothers, a muchacho fanatic, introduced him to the world of martial arts when he was only 5. From that day on, his interests for fighting only grew. From the age of 12 until 16 he practiced taekwondo. After that, he gave jiu-jitsu a chance. “I didn’t like fighting in the floor very much, but Royce Gracie’s career was exploding at the moment, so I decided to take classes during school vacation and ended up falling in love with it.”
 
At TUF’s house Magrão is experimenting a mix of feelings. He is living the anxiety of participating in the competition, as well as the expectation for the birth of his first child, that is supposed to happen while he is still in the house. “I know that if I do well on the competition and reach the finals, I will miss the last moments of my wife’s pregnancy. But we also know that this situation gives me even more energy to win”, he grasps. He only fears that his wife watches the fights. “She better not, otherwise she’ll be way too nervous.”
 
About being one of the integrants of TUF Brasil, Magrão doesn’t hide the anxiety of the first fight and the many challenges after that. “I must say that I was anxious to go in. The moment I crossed the corridor to enter the octagon was brutal. Wen I saw the arena and the people from the athletic comission, I had a little taste of what’s like to be on UFC and live my dream. 
 
Magrão admires Dan Handerson and the Gracies, but his real idol is Rodrigo Minotauro. “I’m not complementing them just because I train on his academy – Team Nogueira –, but Minotauro is amazing. He has a big big heart. I had 3 surgeries on my body and sometimes, when the weather is cold, it hurts and I makes me not want to practice. The guy has 28 surgeries, he doesn’t even know what it is like to practice without pain, yet, he is always there”, he says with pride.
Pleased to be on Sonnen’s team, Magrão sees Wanderlei as a myth, but knows that the north-american fighter is an excelent teacher and can do a lot for him.

He is a fan of the heavy metal band Pantera. This is Edgard’s Castaldelli Filho, 34 years old, style. Born in Ribeirão Preto, Magrão, as he likes to be called, was sure he would be a musician nin the future. “There was no other option for me when I was a teen: I wanted to be a professional musician. But yet, I knew nothing about life”, he says.
 
It was the influence of his Brothers that made Magrão drop the artistic life. “I left the beat of the music for MMA’s beating”, he says, with a smile on the face. One of his older Brothers, a muchacho fanatic, introduced him to the world of martial arts when he was only 5. From that day on, his interests for fighting only grew. From the age of 12 until 16 he practiced taekwondo. After that, he gave jiu-jitsu a chance. “I didn’t like fighting in the floor very much, but Royce Gracie’s career was exploding at the moment, so I decided to take classes during school vacation and ended up falling in love with it.”
 
At TUF’s house Magrão is experimenting a mix of feelings. He is living the anxiety of participating in the competition, as well as the expectation for the birth of his first child, that is supposed to happen while he is still in the house. “I know that if I do well on the competition and reach the finals, I will miss the last moments of my wife’s pregnancy. But we also know that this situation gives me even more energy to win”, he grasps. He only fears that his wife watches the fights. “She better not, otherwise she’ll be way too nervous.”
 
 
About being one of the integrants of TUF Brasil, Magrão doesn’t hide the anxiety of the first fight and the many challenges after that. “I must say that I was anxious to go in. The moment I crossed the corridor to enter the octagon was brutal. Wen I saw the arena and the people from the athletic comission, I had a little taste of what’s like to be on UFC and live my dream.
 
Magrão admires Dan Handerson and the Gracies, but his real idol is Rodrigo Minotauro. “I’m not complementing them just because I train on his academy – Team Nogueira –, but Minotauro is amazing. He has a big big heart. I had 3 surgeries on my body and sometimes, when the weather is cold, it hurts and I makes me not want to practice. The guy has 28 surgeries, he doesn’t even know what it is like to practice without pain, yet, he is always there”, he says with pride.

qna.value:
TRAINING: In the morning, three times a week, a long distance run and speed work, and three times a week I work with weights. In the afternoon from Monday to Saturday in alternate days I do boxing, Jiu Jitsu and Wrestling, and according to the phase of the training I mix all of them.

Q&A

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training to fight in 2002 because I always had a dream to become an MMA world champion. Then I went to Salvador city (Bahia - Brazil) looking for master Luiz Dorea in 2003.
What ranks and titles have you held? I am the # 1 in my State, and champion of Minotauro Fights I, II, III, V, Bahia State Boxing Champion 2006, 3rd Place at the Jiu-Jitsu World Championships in 2005.
Do you have any heroes? Minotauro Nogueira and Anderson Silva, who are my training partners in boxing here.
What is your favorite technique? Knockouts and submissions
What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s a dream to be in the best MMA event worldwide; it’s the first step in order for me to conquer my goal, which is to be the best in the world. The world will know the Bahia's crocodile.
Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No
What was your job before you started fighting? I used to work in the plantation to earn some money. In 2003 I met Master Dorea, who I train with. I came to Salvador City and he gave me a place to stay and food. Today I live with him; he is like my second father.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started in 2018, training BJJ to lose some weight, and I really took a liking to it.

What ranks and titles have you held? Double champ of Demo Fight (SW and FW) and FW champ of WS Fighting

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Khabib is my favorite fighter, for his legacy, for his game that never falters, for his lifestyle, and for his mentality.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career? Contender was the realization of my first dream. Contender is the most important.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? A dream come true

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? In amateur MMA, multiple-time Sergipe state BJJ champ

What are your current ranks in martial arts?

  • Brown belt in Jiu-Jitsu
  • Blue belt in Muay Thai
  • Black belt in life


Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I started three different courses but didn’t finish any - Accounting, Dentistry, and Physical Education.

What was your job before you started fighting? I used to work at my mom's emporium; I would do stock check and work as a cashier.

Favorite grappling technique: Rear Naked Choke

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? Of course. I come from a very small town of 8,000 inhabitants with no infrastructure whatsoever, zero education or sports. I want to use my influence for the benefit of children, so that they can have better opportunities for education, sports, and leisure as well. 

Besides a championship or money, what motivates you?
Being proud of my family and my country and influencing women and children.

Favorite Striking technique: Straight right

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: I have a wonderful and very supportive partner in everything, we have a son, he is my stepson but I consider him my son, I have raised him since he was 5 years old, we have 2 dogs, Thor and Goliath, they are our darlings. And thank God I am blessed with this family. I am more of a homebody, I really enjoy watching movies and series, I like hiking and traveling, and whenever I can I eat different food in restaurants, I love to eat.

What is one thing you want UFC fans to know about you? That I am the strongest woman in the world and I will prove it to them, that I made mistakes like any human being, but that I learn from my mistakes and every day I try to correct myself and become a better person!

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training and fighting back in 2020 during Covid. My initial plan was to go play football at a JUCO in California to get more looks, but once Covid hit my pops, I started training. I took two amateur fights that lasted a combined 22 seconds and the rest is history.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? 5-0 with two belts

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Brown belt in BJJ

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighter is Anderson Silva because seeing him fight at his prime it was almost like he was untouchable. A true pioneer of this sport.

What was your job before you started fighting? Working at car dealership

Personal Life / Background: I’m the second youngest out of four siblings, I started wrestling at the age of five, two-time state qualifier, I have a five-year-old. My hobbies are making music, playing volleyball and football, and going on hikes.

Biggest difference in training for this fight? The biggest difference for this training camp leading up to this fight is just the pure intensity and how hard we have been pushing my cardio making sure I’m in the best shape as possible.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started fighting in December of 2022 because I was very angry at the way life was going and I had attempted suicide due to the overwhelming stress of life and I needed an outlet and fighting became that outlet.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I was ranked #1 in my region as a heavyweight amateur fighter.

TRAINING: Lift about 3 times a week at EWU campus, train at Sik-Jitsu twice a day.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started fighting as an outlet for my aggression. I’ve always been attracted to combat sports. I had my first MMA practice a little over three years ago, and have been brawling with Julianna almost every day. And going with her is great; you either stick it out and get tough, or quit.

What ranks and titles have you held? Washington State Amateur champion

Do you have any heroes? My mom, Diane Phillips. She is my major inspiration, as well as the women in MMA before that have paved the way for me to do what I love.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means a lot of things - it means I can make this a career, I can make a name for myself, and hopefully be a role model for the younger generation of female fighters.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I have an Applied Science degree and am currently at Eastern Washington University.  I’m only 1 quarter away from graduating.

What was your job before you started fighting? Personal athletic trainer

Favorite grappling technique: Guillotine

Favorite striking technique: Overhand right
